title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: St Barbara Personnel
tiers.description: All individuals at all levels who are employed by, act for, or represent St Barbara anywhere in the world: directors, officers, managers, employees, contractors, consultants, agents and anyone else representing or acting on behalf of St Barbara, irrespective of employment status.

tiers.name: Designated Employees
tiers.description: Directors, Executives, Key Management Personnel (AASB 124), the General Counsel and Company Secretary, Senior managers, and anyone else designated by the Chair, Managing Director & CEO or General Counsel and Company Secretary by virtue of their position, role, activities or information available to them.

tiers.name: Director of St Barbara
tiers.description: A director who is a Designated Employee; distinguished only for the identity of the clearance approvers.

tiers.name: Chair of St Barbara
tiers.description: The Chair, distinguished only for the identity of the clearance approvers.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Spouse/partner, parents or children (incl. step-children), a relative sharing the household 12+ months, a business partner of the person or of any Connected Person, a company/entity where the person is a director/officer/senior executive or holds >20%, a trustee of a trust where the person or a Connected Person is a beneficiary, and any 'associate' or 'related party' under the Corporations Act.

definitions.hedging_definition: the use by any St Barbara Personnel of any derivative product or hedging in relation to St Barbara Securities designed to limit the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel

windows.end_anchor: end of the ASX trading session on the Business Day following the public release of St Barbara's March Quarterly Report in April
end of the ASX trading session on the Business Day following the public release of St Barbara's preliminary or final full year results in August
end of the ASX trading session on the Business Day following the public release of St Barbara's September Quarterly Report in October
end of the ASX trading session on the Business Day following the public release of St Barbara's half year results in February

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Managing Director & CEO (as its delegate) may determine in writing that a Blackout Period be extended (not shortened) or a new Blackout Period introduced. Confidential: 'The fact that a Blackout Period has been extended or a new Blackout Period has been imposed, is strictly confidential to St Barbara.'

rules.detail: Blanket ban on any derivative product (caps, collars, warrants, options) designed to limit economic risk in St Barbara Securities, applying to all personnel regardless of vesting status; there is no clearance carve-out for this prohibition.
rules.evidence: the use by any St Barbara Personnel of any derivative product or hedging in relation to St Barbara Securities designed to limit the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel is prohibited.

rules.detail: Narrow carve-out for exchange traded options that are acquired, disposed of and reported, but only if their effect does not limit or reduce the person's economic risk; a collar by definition limits risk and so falls outside this carve-out.
rules.evidence: This prohibition does not extend to exchange traded options in St Barbara Securities which are acquired, disposed of and reported, provided that the effect of those exchange traded options does not limit or reduce the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel.

rules.detail: Same clause as the derivatives prohibition; a purchased put and written call collar is squarely 'hedging ... designed to limit the economic risk' and is banned outright with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: the use by any St Barbara Personnel of any derivative product or hedging in relation to St Barbara Securities designed to limit the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel is prohibited.

rules.detail: Statutory overlay noted in the policy: KMP and closely related parties are separately prohibited by s206J from limiting exposure to risk on unvested remuneration, independent of any policy clearance.
rules.evidence: prohibits a member of key management personnel of St Barbara and their closely related parties from entering into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: a. has not vested in the member

rules.detail: Same statutory overlay extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: b. has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure falls within Dealing limb (f) (a contract securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to price fluctuations) and, because it limits the person's economic risk, is also caught by the section 7.1 hedging ban.
rules.evidence: creating, acquiring or disposing of any other right or obligation, present or future, conditional or unconditional, to acquire or dispose of Securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling St Barbara Securities by any St Barbara Personnel.
rules.evidence: As a consequence, Short Selling by any St Barbara Personnel in relation to St Barbara Securities is prohibited.

rules.detail: Securities lending is expressly named within the Dealing definition, so it is subject to the general insider trading prohibition and Blackout Periods, but non-Designated Employees need no specific clearance to do it outside a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: entering into an arrangement or acting to transfer the beneficial or underlying ownership of Securities (including a Securities lending arrangement)

rules.detail: As a Dealing, a securities lending arrangement by a Designated Employee requires a written Clearance Notice before it can occur.
rules.evidence: A Designated Employee and their Connected Persons must not Deal in St Barbara Securities ... unless the Designated Employee has obtained a written notice authorising them to do so (Clearance Notice).

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over St Barbara shares is a contract securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to price fluctuations (Dealing limb (f)) and, to the extent it limits the holder's economic risk, is also caught by the section 7.1 hedging ban.
rules.evidence: entering into a contract or other arrangement with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to price fluctuations in Securities

rules.detail: Not prohibited. Any St Barbara Personnel proposing a margin loan over their shares must give the lender a copy of the Policy before entering into it; no clearance is required unless the person is a Designated Employee.
rules.evidence: Any St Barbara Personnel who proposes to use their St Barbara Securities as collateral or enter into a margin loan in relation to their St Barbara Securities, must provide a copy of this Policy to the lender before providing the St Barbara Securities as collateral or entering into the margin loan.

rules.detail: A Designated Employee may margin loan their shares only after obtaining lender confirmation that the shares will not be sold in contravention of the employee's obligations, and prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: a Designated Employee is not permitted to use their St Barbara Securities as collateral or to enter into a margin loan or similar arrangement in relation to them, without: a. obtaining confirmation from the lender or holder of the collateral that the St Barbara Securities will not be sold or disposed of by it in contravention of the Designated Employee's obligations under this Policy; and b. seeking and obtaining, in writing, formal clearance

rules.detail: Granting security/collateral over shares is expressly addressed (not banned): a copy of the Policy must be given to the lender before the shares are pledged.
rules.evidence: Any St Barbara Personnel who proposes to use their St Barbara Securities as collateral ... must provide a copy of this Policy to the lender before providing the St Barbara Securities as collateral

rules.detail: Designated Employees need lender confirmation plus prior written clearance before granting security over their shares.
rules.evidence: a Designated Employee is not permitted to use their St Barbara Securities as collateral ... without: a. obtaining confirmation from the lender or holder of the collateral that the St Barbara Securities will not be sold or disposed of by it in contravention of the Designated Employee's obligations under this Policy; and b. seeking and obtaining, in writing, formal clearance

rules.detail: Secured financing generally (collateral, margin loan or 'similar arrangement') is not prohibited; the only condition on non-Designated Employees is giving the lender a copy of the Policy first.
rules.evidence: use their St Barbara Securities as collateral or enter into a margin loan or similar arrangement in relation to them

rules.detail: Designated Employees require lender confirmation and prior written clearance before entering any secured financing arrangement over their shares; the loan leg of a collar is structurally available for this tier, unlike the option legs.
rules.evidence: a Designated Employee is not permitted to use their St Barbara Securities as collateral or to enter into a margin loan or similar arrangement in relation to them, without ... seeking and obtaining, in writing, formal clearance

rules.detail: No dealing in the same securities within any 3 month period, except that securities granted as remuneration under an employee share scheme are exempt once vested. Note: section 6.2 refers inconsistently to 'the 12 month period referred to in section 4.3', though section 4.3 itself states a 3 month period.
rules.evidence: Accordingly, St Barbara Personnel must not Deal with the same St Barbara Securities within any 3 month period.

clearance.evidence: A St Barbara Personnel who is not a Designated Employee, is not required to seek any specific or written approval to Deal in St Barbara Securities, provided any such Dealing occurs outside of a Blackout Period and is otherwise in accordance with this Policy.

clearance.approver: Chair and the General Counsel and Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: General Counsel and Company Secretary (Form B)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 3 days of the Dealing taking place
clearance.evidence: Director of St Barbara: Both the Chair and the General Counsel and Company Secretary. ... the Dealing may only occur within 5 Business Days of the date of the Clearance Notice (or such other period as may be specified in the Clearance Notice).

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit Committee and the Managing Director & CEO
clearance.post_trade_to: General Counsel and Company Secretary (Form B)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 3 days of the Dealing taking place
clearance.evidence: Chair of St Barbara: Both the Chair of the Audit Committee and the Managing Director & CEO.

clearance.approver: Managing Director & CEO and the General Counsel and Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: General Counsel and Company Secretary (Form B)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 3 days of the Dealing taking place
clearance.evidence: All other Designated Employees: Both the Managing Director & CEO and the General Counsel and Company Secretary. A Clearance Notice may be given or refused by the persons listed in the table above, in their absolute discretion, without the need to provide reasons.

carve_outs: St Barbara Securities granted to St Barbara Personnel as part of their remuneration which have vested in accordance with the terms of the relevant employee share scheme
short_term.evidence: St Barbara Personnel must not Deal with the same St Barbara Securities within any 3 month period.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of St Barbara Securities between St Barbara Personnel and their respective Connected Persons (or among Connected Persons);
transfers of St Barbara Securities already held by a St Barbara Personnel into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which that St Barbara Personnel or a Connected Person is a beneficiary;

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in St Barbara Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party who is not a Connected Person or a St Barbara Personnel;

where a St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person is a trustee, trading in St Barbara Securities by that trust, provided neither the St Barbara Personnel nor any Connected Person is a beneficiary of the trust and the decision to trade was taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer, and disposals of St Barbara Securities pursuant to a scheme of arrangement;
disposals of rights under a pro rata offer;
acquisitions of St Barbara Securities under a pro rata issue (i.e., on exercise of rights), and allowing rights acquired under a pro rata issue to lapse;

acquisitions under a security purchase plan offered by St Barbara or a dividend reinvestment plan where the person does not commence or amend participation during a prohibited period and the plan does not permit withdrawal during a prohibited period;
disposals of St Barbara Securities under an equal access buy-back;

subject to the St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person having complied with section 7.2 of this Policy, a disposal of St Barbara Securities by a secured lender without the permission or authority of the St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person at the time that is the result of that lender exercising its rights under a lending arrangement;
the exercise (but not the sale of St Barbara Securities following exercise) of an option or vesting of a right under an employee incentive scheme;

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan (but which does not include sales under stop/loss orders) for which prior written clearance has been provided ... where ... the trading plan does not permit the St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director & CEO (Board, if the affected person is the Managing Director & CEO)
exceptions.evidence: is in severe financial hardship; or

exceptions.approver: Managing Director & CEO (Board, if the affected person is the Managing Director & CEO)
exceptions.evidence: is required by a court order or some other overriding legal or regulator requirement to sell or dispose of St Barbara Securities.

financing_disclosure: St Barbara Personnel (general): trigger inception (before providing shares as collateral or entering a margin loan), to the lender, deadline before the collateral/loan is entered into.

Designated Employees: trigger inception, to the lender (confirmation the shares will not be sold in breach of the Policy) and to the clearance approvers (Chair/CEO/GC per role), deadline before entering into the collateralisation, margin loan or arrangement.

external_documents: Rules of the relevant employee share scheme (St Barbara Limited Employee Share Plan, Performance Rights Plan, Non-Executive Director Share Plan, Short Term Incentive Share Scheme)
exemption_authority: Managing Director & CEO (or the Board, if the affected person is the Managing Director & CEO) may determine in their sole and absolute discretion, without giving reasons, that 'Exceptional Circumstances' (severe financial hardship, or a court order/overriding legal or regulatory requirement) permit a sale or disposal (not purchase) during a Blackout Period or the short-term dealing period. A general tax liability, a tax liability on incentive scheme securities, or an obligation to sell under a collateralisation arrangement expressly will NOT constitute Exceptional Circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the use by any St Barbara Personnel of any derivative product or hedging in relation to St Barbara Securities designed to limit the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel is prohibited.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This clearance-proof, tier-blind ban prohibits both legs of an OTC collar (purchased put and written call) outright, regardless of vesting state, tier, or any clearance obtained, and has no exemption authority capable of overriding it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition does not extend to exchange traded options in St Barbara Securities which are acquired, disposed of and reported, provided that the effect of those exchange traded options does not limit or reduce the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Too narrow to help: a collar is designed precisely to limit/reduce economic risk, so it falls outside this carve-out even if exchange-traded.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Employees may also be subject to a statutory prohibition in section 206J of the Corporations Act, which prohibits a member of key management personnel of St Barbara and their closely related parties from entering into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An independent statutory prohibition for KMP on unvested/locked incentive securities cannot be waived by any policy clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a Designated Employee is not permitted to use their St Barbara Securities as collateral or to enter into a margin loan or similar arrangement ... without: a. obtaining confirmation from the lender ... that the St Barbara Securities will not be sold or disposed of by it in contravention of the Designated Employee's obligations under this Policy; and b. seeking and obtaining, in writing, formal clearance
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The secured-loan leg of a funded collar is structurally available (unlike the option legs) for Designated Employees who obtain lender confirmation and written clearance, and for other personnel merely by giving the lender a copy of the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to the St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person having complied with section 7.2 of this Policy, a disposal of St Barbara Securities by a secured lender without the permission or authority of the St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person ... that is the result of that lender exercising its rights under a lending arrangement [is excluded from the Policy and may be undertaken] at any time, without prior written clearance
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the loan (not the banned option legs) were ever put in place compliantly, a lender's enforcement sale on default would not itself breach the Policy or need fresh clearance, even inside a Blackout Period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: voluntary margin-call sale gets no hardship relief
bespoke_clauses.clause: a general tax liability, a tax liability relating to St Barbara Securities received under an employee incentive scheme or an obligation to sell under a collateralisation arrangement will not constitute Exceptional Circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the executive (rather than the lender) needs to sell to meet a margin call, no hardship exemption is available; the sale must still wait out any Blackout Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Clearance Notice may be given or refused by the persons listed in the table above, in their absolute discretion, without the need to provide reasons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for the permitted loan leg, approval is not guaranteed and the bank cannot treat clearance as a formality.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the 12 month period referred to in section 4.3 [section 6.2] vs. 'within any 3 month period' [section 4.3]; the ASX cover letter notes the prior version lodged 3 June 2026 'contained errors in section 4.3'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The short-term dealing period is internally inconsistent following a recent, imperfect amendment; confirm the current 3- or 12-month figure directly with the company before relying on it for collar tenor.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Dealings by Directors of St Barbara or any of their associates ... must be disclosed to the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) as required by Listing Rule 3.19A ... to report changes in a Director's holding within five (5) Business Days of a change occurring.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted secured-loan leg entered into by a director becomes public within 5 business days, limiting confidentiality of the financing arrangement.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar cannot be implemented under this policy because section 7.1 imposes a blanket, clearance-proof prohibition on any derivative product or hedging designed to limit a person's economic risk in St Barbara securities, which squarely catches a purchased put and written call collar for every tier and every vesting state, and is reinforced for KMP by the statutory section 206J overlay on unvested or holding-locked remuneration. There is no exemption authority, hardship carve-out or clearance route capable of authorising the option legs. By contrast, the loan leg is comparatively permissive: a Designated Employee may pledge or margin-loan their shares provided the lender is given a copy of the Policy and, before the arrangement is entered into, confirms it will not sell in breach of the Policy and the employee obtains written clearance, while a subsequent lender enforcement sale is an excluded dealing needing no fresh approval. However, because the derivative legs cannot be written or purchased at all, the loan alone cannot support a genuine collar structure, and a voluntary sale by the executive to meet a margin call receives no hardship relief and must still respect Blackout Periods. The bank could therefore offer only a secured loan against vested shares (with lender confirmations and clearance), not the collar itself, unless the company grants a bespoke policy waiver.
